properties.Report_Name: Karangetang (Indonesia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) and a news source reported that an eruption at Karangetang?s North Crater (Kawah Dua) continued during 27 August-2 September. Daily white plumes rose as high as 500 m above the summit and drifted in various directions. Incandescence at the North Crater and from lava flows and/or incandescent avalanches on the flanks was visible in some webcam images throughout the week. Seismicity remained at high levels and rumbling sounds were occasionally heard. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was advised to stay 1.5 km away from both craters, with an extension to 2.5 km on the NW and SW flanks of North Crater. 
 Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)
properties.Report_Source: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report

properties.Report_Name: Klyuchevskoy (Russia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that the eruption at Klyuchevskoy continued at the summit crater during 27 August-2 September. A daily thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images. Daily ash plumes rose as high as 7 km (23,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted as far as 170 km NE and E during 27-30 August. The Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale). Dates are based on UTC; specific events are in local time where noted. 
 Source: Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT)

properties.Report_Name: Krakatau (Indonesia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Krakatau during 27 August-2 September. Ash-and-gas plumes that were a mixture of white, gray, and black colors rose 100-400 m above the summit and drifted mainly W, NW, N, and NE during 27-31 August. A webcam image on 27 August showed incandescent material being ejected above the crater. White plumes were visible rising as high as 200 m and drifting SW, W, and NW during 1-2 September. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was advised to stay 3 km away from summit. 
 Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

properties.Report_Name: Ranakah (Indonesia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - New Unrest
properties.Report_Summary:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported increased unrest at Ranakah. Following the M 7.7 tectonic earthquake that occurred off the N coast Flores Island on 15 August there was an increase in the overall number of daily tectonic events. The number of deep volcanic earthquakes also increased, up to 35 events per day. Seismicity declined but remained high towards the end of August, until 1 September when over 100 deep volcanic earthquakes were recorded. Drone overflights revealed denser plumes rising from the solfataras W of the lava dome on 25 August and more diffuse plumes rising from the same area on 1 September. No significant changes at the lava dome were observed during the overflights despite earthquake-triggered landslides occurring in several areas at Ranakah on 18 and 20 August. At 2300 on 1 September the Alert Level was raised to 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 1 km away from the crater. 
 Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)
properties.Report_Source: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report

properties.Report_Name: Sinabung (Indonesia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that after a period of escalating unrest at Sinabung, which had been detected at least since May, a new eruption occurred on 31 August. During 1-30 August white-and-gray plumes rose as high as 1 km above the summit. Observers noted that the vegetation on the E flank yellowed and dried out. The seismic network recorded a total of one rockfall event, 14 earthquakes indicating emissions, two tornillo earthquakes, 29 low-frequency earthquakes, eight hybrid/multi-phase earthquakes, one shallow volcanic earthquake, and 141 deep volcanic earthquakes. On 28 August blue plumes descending the SE flank were observed. 
  
Prior to the eruption on 31 August a swarm was detected that consisted of 85 volcanic earthquakes, one earthquake indicating an emission, and one harmonic tremor. At 1017 a dense black ash plume rose around 3.5 km above the summit and drifted E and SE. The eruption lasted just over an hour based on seismic data. At 1230 the Alert Level was raised to 3 (the second highest level on a scale of 1-4). Though most of the exclusion zone remained at 3 km from the summit, it was increased to 6 km on the SE flank. Hotspots on the N flank were visible. According to a news source ashfall was reported in Berastagi City and residents were urged to wear masks while outside to avoid breathing in ash. Schools in high-risk areas implemented virtual learning for one day.
  
Later that day, during 1800-2400, dense gray-and-brown plumes rose 200-500 m above the summit and drifted NE and E. On 1 September white-and-gray ash plumes rose as high as 600 m above the summit and drifted E, SE, and S, causing ashfall in areas to the SE. News sources reported that residents of Kuta Tengah Village and Payung Village (5 km SSW) were preemptively moved to evacuation centers following increased volcanic activity. Two flights on the Banda Aceh-Medan route were affected, one delayed and one canceled, due to ash in the air. At 0720 on 2 September a gray-to-brown ash plume rose about 1 km above the summit and drifted E and SE.
 
 Sources: Antara News,Antara News,Antara News,Antara News,Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)
properties.Report_Source: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report

properties.Report_Name: Aira (Japan) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Minamidake Crater (Aira Caldera?s Sakurajima volcano) during 24-31 August. Crater incandescence was visible in nighttime webcam images during 24-28 August. An explosion at 0951 on 25 August generated an ash plume that rose 400 n above the summit, into weather clouds. Volcanologists conducted a field survey on 27 August and measured very high sulfur dioxide emissions, averaging 3,400 tons per day. There were 22 eruptive events recorded during 28-31 August generating ash plumes that rose as high as 2 km above the crater rim. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a 5-level scale), and the public was warned to be cautious within 1 km of both the Minimadake and Showa craters. 
 Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)

properties.Report_Name: Ambae (Vanuatu) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Vanuatu Meteorology and Geohazards Department (VMGD) and the Wellington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that the eruption at Ambae continued during 27 August-2 September. According to the VAAC multiple daily plumes during 27-30 August were identified in satellite data and webcam images rising 1.5-7.6 km (5,000-25,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifting W, SE, and E. An ash plume rose to 12.5 km (41,000 ft) a.s.l. on 1 September and drifted ESE. VMGD noted that the ash plume also contained very high amounts of sulfur dioxide. Ashfall was reported in areas to the N, E, and S parts of the island, and reached the N part of Pentecost Island. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 0-5), and the public was warned to stay outside of Danger Zone B, defined as a 3-km radius around the active vents in Lake Voui, and to stay away from drainages during heavy rains. 
 Sources: Vanuatu Meteorology and Geohazards Department (VMGD),Wellington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC)

properties.Report_Summary:
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that unrest at Asosan showed a downward trend since 17 August based on seismic and gas emission data. At 1600 on 1 September the Alert Level was lowered to 2 (on a scale of 1-5) and the public was warned not to enter the area around the crater.  
 Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)

properties.Report_Name: Etna (Italy) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported that eruptive activity at Etna?s summit craters during 24-30 August was characterized by gas emissions and periodic minor ash emissions at Northeast Crater, and minor gas emissions at Southeast Crater. The volcano Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) according to the Dipartimento della Protezione Civile. 
 Source: Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV)

properties.Report_Name: Great Sitkin (United States) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO) reported that slow lava effusion continued to feed a thick flow in Great Sitkin?s summit crater during 27 August-2 September based on webcam and satellite images. The flow gradually expanded E. Minor earthquakes were detected daily, likely associated with rockfalls on the growing dome. Weather clouds obscured webcam and satellite views during most of the week. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Watch (the third level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the third color on a four-color scale). 
 Source: US Geological Survey Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO)

properties.Report_Name: Ibu (Indonesia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Ibu continued during 27 August-2 September, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Gray ash plumes rose 300-800 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions, especially towards the N, NE, and SE. Incandescence at the summit was visible in some nighttime webcam images. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the public was advised to stay 2 km away from the active crater and 3.5 km away from the N crater wall opening.

properties.Report_Summary:
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that unrest at Iwatesan had ceased. Deformation detected by multiple methods had stopped and seismicity was at a low level. At 1100 on 27 August the Alert Level was lowered to 1 (the lowest level on a 1-5 scale).  
 Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)

properties.Report_Name: Kilauea (United States) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by episodic fountaining, incandescence, and intermittent spatter from craters along the SW margin of Halema`uma`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 27 August-2 September. Incandescence or flaming at the N vent was periodically recorded in webcam images. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Advisory (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code remained at Yellow (the second lowest color on a four-color scale). 
 Source: US Geological Survey Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO)

The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that eruptive activity continued at Lewotobi Laki-Laki during 27 August-2 September. At 0830 on 27 August a gray ash plume rose 2.5 km above the summit and drifted SW and W. According to a news source the eruption lasted just over two minutes and was accompanied by a booming sound. From that time through 31 August daily ash plumes rose 200-700 m above the summit and drifted NW, W, and SW. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4), and the public was warned to stay 5 km away from the center of Laki-Laki.

properties.Report_Name: Lewotolok (Indonesia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported continuing eruptive activity at Lewotolok during 27 August-2 September. Daily ash plumes with various color combinations of white, gray, and black were visible rising 300-800 m above the summit and drifting NW and W. The lava flow on the SSE flank had lengthened to 1.8 km by the beginning of the week and did not advance by the end of the week. A lava flow on the NE flank was 600 m long and advanced to 1.1 km long by 1 September. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4). The public was warned to stay 2 km away from the summit with an extension to 3 km on the S and SE flanks. 
 Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

properties.Report_Name: Mayon (Philippines) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported that the eruption at Mayon continued at low levels during 27 August-2 September. Each day the seismic network recorded 6-26 volcanic earthquakes. Sulfur dioxide emissions (SO?) averaged 5,005-5,878 tonnes per day (t/d) during 26-30 August, peaked at a very high rate of 7,115 t/d on 31 August, and then slightly decreased to 6,981 and 6,931 t/d on 1 and 2 September, respectively. SO? emission had averaged 3,844 t/d since the Alert level was lowered to 2 on 5 August. 
  
Six ash emissions, each lasting as long as 47 minutes, were recorded on 26 August; emissions rose as high as 1 km and drifted ESE. A weak explosion at 0900 on 27 August generated a grayish ash plume that rose 500 m above the summit and drifted ENE. The event lasted about one minute. At 0908 on 28 August a grayish ash plume rose 150 m above the summit and drifted ENE. On 30 August an ash emission was recorded for about one minute. Weather clouds obscured views on the other days. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a 0-5 scale) and the public was reminded to stay away from the 6-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ). PHIVOLCS recommended that civil aviation authorities advise pilots to avoid flying close to the summit.
 
 Source: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS)
properties.Report_Source: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report

properties.Report_Name: Poas (Costa Rica) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Observatorio Vulcanológico y Sismológico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA) reported several small eruptions at Poás during 27 August-2 September with a few notable events. An eruption at 0235 on 27 August was comprised of two pulses based on seismic and acoustic data. The event ejected incandescent ballistics 600 m from the crater onto the E terrace. An eruptive event at 0048 on 2 September produced a small ash plume. The Volcanic Alert Level remained at 2 (the second lowest level on a four-level scale). 
 Source: Observatorio Vulcanologico y Sismologico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA)

properties.Report_Name: Purace (Colombia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Servicio Geologico Colombiano (SGC) reported intensifying eruptive activity at Puracé during 26 August-2 September. Signals associated with fluid movement dominated the seismicity and were characterized as tremor-type signals and, to a lesser extent, long-period events located beneath Puracé volcano at depths less than 2 km. Sulfur dioxide flux stayed above the average baseline level, averaging 760 tonnes per day (t/d) on 27 August and 1,338 t/d on 26 August. Soil carbon dioxide concentrations rose throughout the reporting period. Slow ground deformation persisted in an area between the Puracé, Piocollo, and Curiquinga volcanoes. As many as eight daily ash emissions were recorded by the seismic network, though adverse weather conditions often prevented visual confirmation. Ash emissions rose as high as 3,250 m above the summit during 26-27 August. Eruption noises and ashfall were reported in the town center of Coconuco, Cristales, Campamento, and 20 de Julio, in the municipality of Coconuco. During 28-29 August ashfall was reported in the villages of Chiligló, Alto de Anambío (7 km NW), and Cristales, in the municipality of Puracé. Ash plumes rose up to 240 m above the summit during 31 August-1 September.
  
Seismic activity associated with rock fracturing (volcano-tectonic earthquakes, VT) was low in both number and magnitude, with signals located beneath Piocollo and Puracé at depths less than 4 km. Beginning at 1620 on 29 August, however, both the number and magnitude of VT earthquakes increased and by 1500 on 30 August the seismic network recorded 472 events. They were mainly located 10-15 km NE of Puracé volcano at depths of 6-12 km. There were 18 events with magnitudes equal or great than 2, with the largest a M 4.3, and at least seven were felt by residents in the municipalities of Puracé, Totoró, Sotará, and Popayán. About 150 more VT events were recorded by the afternoon of 31 August, and around 180 more by the early afternoon of 2 September, all located in a similar area, and a few felt by residents. The Alert Level remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale).
 
 Source: Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC)

properties.Report_Name: Rincon de la Vieja (Costa Rica) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Observatorio Vulcanológico y Sismológico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA) reported that small phreatic eruptions at Rincón de la Vieja were recorded daily by the seismic and infrasound networks during 26 August-2 September. A total of 20 phreatic eruptions were detected from the morning of 28 August to 0512 on 1 September, with eight of those generating lahars on the flanks. The most energetic event occurred at 1637 on 31 August and also produced a steam plume that rose 1 km. The Alert Level remained at 3 (Caution) and the Aviation Color Code remained Orange. 
 Source: Observatorio Vulcanologico y Sismologico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA)
properties.Report_Source: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report

properties.Report_Name: Sabancaya (Peru) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Instituto Geofísico del Perú?s (IGP) Centro Vulcanológico Nacional (CENVUL) reported continuing eruptive activity at Sabancaya during 24-30 August. The seismic network detected 71 seismic events associated with the movement of magmatic fluids, along with earthquakes indicating internal rock fracturing; no volcanic explosions occurred during the period. Gas, steam, and ash emissions periodically rose as high as 900 m above the summit and drifted less than 10 km NE, E, and SE. Moderate sulfur dioxide (SO?) emissions averaged 1,138 tons per day, and nine thermal anomalies (each 2 MW or less) associated with the lava dome were identified. The Alert Level remained at Orange (the third level on a four-color scale) and the public was warned to stay outside of a 12 km radius from the summit. 
 Source: Instituto Geofísico del Perú (IGP)

properties.Report_Name: Semeru (Indonesia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity continued at Semeru during 27-2 September, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. White-and-gray ash plumes rose 300-1,000 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions during 27-29 August and 31 August-2 September. The Alert Level remained at 3 (the second highest level on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay at least 5 km away from the Jonggring Saloko Crater in all directions, 13 km from the summit on the SE flank along the Kobokan drainage, and 500 m from the banks of the Kobokan drainage as far as 17 km SE of the summit. 
 Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

properties.Report_Name: Sheveluch (Russia) - Report for 27 August-2 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
properties.Report_Summary:
The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported continuing lava effusion and explosive activity at the lava domes along the N crater floor of Young Sheveluch (on the SW flank of Old Sheveluch) during 27 August-2 September. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on most days; weather clouds occasionally obscured views. The Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale). Dates are based on UTC; specific events are in local time where noted. 
 Source: Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT)
